subject: Demo follow-up: prioritized candidate slate and sprint asks
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julie Park <julie@acme.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 May 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap + candidate engines for Acme pilot

Hi Julie —

Thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap and suggested next moves so we keep momentum heading into the pilot planning: 

What we heard (short):
- Primary SLA: 95th pct latency <= 350ms for single-turn chat at 512 tokens.
- Quality bar: <3% semantic regressions vs your current baseline on the 10k customer-support eval set.
- Cost target: ~60% of current per-conversation cost or better over expected volume profile.

Attached: a CSV with the benchmark slices we ran during the demo and the prompt set we used (prompt_set_v1.txt). Link to the full Drive folder below.

Recommended immediate next steps: 
1) Red team/ops: confirm regulatory log retention rules and any redaction needs (we noted this in the tech questionnaire).
2) Pilot slate: run a 2-week compare across 3 candidate inference engines with the provided prompt set + their trimmed eval slices (we propose a staged roll: Litmus -> Balanced -> Speed).
3) Align on mutual action plan (attached PDF) and kick a 2-week operational sprint to produce pass/fail go/no-go on latency + regression guards.

I'd like to propose names for the 3 candidates and the rationale in a single doc — Ben will follow up with scorecards and a short cost/latency/quality matrix. Can we get time for a 30m technical deep dive this week?

Thanks —
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0183
Redwood Inference

From: Julie Park <julie@acme.ai>

Thanks, Evelyn — this is helpful. A couple quick questions before we lock the deep dive: 

- For the latency target: is the 350ms figure end-to-end (our app + network) or server-side only? We need clarity since our client SDK adds ~60ms.
- On regressions: what metric did you use to flag semantic regressions during the demo? We saw a couple of hallucinations in the example thread and want to know how you quantify them.

We're available Thurs morning PT for a technical call (11am PST works). Also — can you confirm whether the cost projections in the CSV reflect quantized variants or FP16 runs? Our procurement team will need that detail for budget planning.

Julie Park
Head of ML Product, Acme.ai
julie@acme.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julie Park <julie@acme.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 11:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: prioritized candidate slate and sprint asks

Julie / team —

Appreciate the quick read. Short answers up front, then proposed slate with rationale: 

Latency figure: the 350ms target in the demo notes was server-side 95th pct (model + inference runtime). We'll add a 60ms client SDK buffer to show expected end-to-end numbers in the spreadsheet.

Regression metric: we used a hybrid approach during the demo: automated semantic similarity (embedding cosine) + human spot checks on 1,200 hard-slice examples. An automated regression is flagged when similarity to baseline < 0.72 and a human labeler marks the response as incorrect/unsafe. The CSV includes the thresholds and per-slice counts.

Cost inputs: the CSV rows currently show two modes — FP16 and 8-bit quantized runtimes. We annotated which rows are quantized. The quick takeaway: the quantized variants reduce GPU token cost by ~30% on average but add ~6–10% variance in correctness on some entity-heavy slices.

Proposed prioritized candidate slate (short):
- Candidate A (Balanced): Moderate quantization, best quality parity (regressions ~1.8%), median server-side 95th pct latency ~280ms. Good default for customer-facing chat.
- Candidate B (Economy): Heavier quantization + KV-cache tuning, best cost (est. 55% of current cost) but higher regressions on entity slices (~3.5%) and 95th pct latency ~240ms. Suggest only if Acme accepts a governance rule for entity redaction/verification.
- Candidate C (Speed-first): Lower-parameter variant, minimal quantization, best p95 latency (~190ms server-side) but worse on long-context quality and ~2.8% regression. Good for throughput-heavy internal routing.

Next ops asks for the 2-week pilot sprint: 
1) We run all three candidates on the prompt_set_v1.txt across the full 10k eval split.
2) Track per-slice regressions + per-variant cost and p95 latency.
3) Set clear go/no-go gates: p95 <= 350ms + regressions <= 3% overall; for entity-heavy slices, require per-slice regression <= 4% or flagged mitigation.

Soojin and I can own the sprint runs and will post daily short snapshots to the Drive folder. Evelyn — if you confirm the Thurs 11am PST call, we’ll bring the scorecards and a short jitter/cold-start breakdown.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Julie —

Confirmed for Thurs 11am PST. Agenda for the 30m: 
- Quick recap of SLA/quality gates (5m)
- Ben: prioritized slate + scorecard walkthrough (10m)
- Soojin: planned runbook & data access needs for the sprint (10m)
- Agree on go/no-go gates and ownership (5m)

One operational note: we will provision a staging Dedicated cluster for the 2-week runs and surface daily token-level costs. Expect two buckets in the cost export: quantized vs FP16. I’ll send calendar invite in a minute and attach an updated mutual action plan that includes a procurement checkpoint mid-sprint.

Looking forward —
Evelyn

Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
